Headteacher's Welcome
At Islamia Primary School we welcome students from all backgrounds and hope to enrich their lives through academic study and a values-laden curriculum enshrined within a strong Islamic ethos which promotes excellent character.
As Headteacher of Islamia Primary School, I am very proud of our students, their achievements and the desire of all those at the school to reach their full potential
السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ
It is a great pleasure to welcome you to Islamia Primary School, a school with a strong Islamic identity and a wonderfully diverse community.
Islamia is a special place, full of learning, faith, friendship and opportunity, where children feel safe, valued and that they belong.
Our aspiration is simple: to build something beautiful together. We provide an excellent education that inspires curiosity, awe and wonder, encouraging children to recognise the signs of Allah in His creation, explore the world around them and develop a lifelong love of learning. We want every child to flourish academically, spiritually and morally, grounded in their dīn and character while developing the confidence and skills they need for the future.
We believe that great schools are built through partnership. By working closely with our families and wider community, we seek to create an environment in which every child can belong, flourish and succeed.
You are warmly invited to visit our school and experience what makes Islamia special. We look forward to welcoming you.

News & Events
The Children's Toothbrushing Guide
Dear Parents and Carers, We are pleased to share the launch of the new Children’s Toothbrushing Guide, created to help families build strong, healthy oral hygiene habits from an early age. Developed in collaboration with early years professionals, the British Society of Paediatric Dentistry and the Oral Health Foundation, this guide provides clear, trusted advice to support children’s oral health right from the start. Why this matters: Tooth decay remains the leading cause of hospital admissions for children aged 5–9, and establishing good brushing habits early can make a lasting difference. The guide includes helpful information such as: 🦷 When and how to brush young children’s teeth 🦷 Practical tips for building brushing into daily routines 🦷 Additional ways to maintain good oral health 🦷 Inclusive guidance for families of children with SEND It is a simple, accessible resource that you can use at home to support happy and healthy smiles. Thank you for your continued support in helping children build healthy habits for life.
Free Children’s Toothbrushing Guide for schools & parents 🦷

News & Events
Mobile Farm Visit
We had a visit from a mobile farm. This unique educational experience brought the wonders of the farm directly to our school, allowing children to engage with animals and learn about them in a fun and interactive way. The mobile farm provided an array of farm animals; including sheep, goats, rabbits, and chickens for the children to meet and learn about. Experienced handlers were on hand to ensure a safe and informative experience. This was a wonderful opportunity for students to gain hands-on learning and develop a deeper understanding of nature and animal care.

Safeguarding
Islamia Primary School is fully committed to safeguarding the welfare of all children and young people by taking all reasonable steps to protect them from neglect, physical, sexual or emotional harm.
Staff and volunteers will at all times show respect and understanding for the rights, safety, and welfare of all service users and conduct themselves in a way that reflects the principles of our school and academy trust.
ensuring that all of our staff and volunteers are carefully selected, trained and supervised;
assessing all risk carefully that children and young people encounter and taking all necessary steps to minimise and manage them;
letting parents and children and young people know how to voice concerns or complaints about anything that they may not be happy with;
giving parents, children and young people and workers information about what we do and what can be expected from us.
requiring clubs, societies, groups using school facilities, to have and abide by their own code, policies, and procedures which a copy must be shown to us;
responding to allegations appropriately with a full investigation and, if appropriate, implement the disciplinary and appeals procedures;
to develop and implement an appropriate monitoring and review system to ensure compliance with the school's Child Protection Policy and Procedures.
Brent Family Front Door
Peer on Peer Sexual Abuse and Harassment
Peer on peer sexual abuse and harassment This helpline provides both children and adults who are potential victims of sexual abuse in schools with the appropriate support and advice. This includes how to contact the police and report crimes if they wish. The helpline also provides support to parents and professionals. See section 21 on our safeguarding policy for our procedures.
Peer on peer sexual abuse and harassment is not acceptable and not tolerated. Sexual harassment refers to unwanted conduct of a sexual nature that occurs online or offline. Sexual harassment violates a pupil’s dignity and makes them feel intimidated, degraded or humiliated, and can create a hostile, sexualised or offensive environment. If left unchallenged, sexual harassment can create an atmosphere that normalises inappropriate behaviour and may lead to sexual violence.
'STOP IT NOW' are a child protection charity who work to prevent child sexual abuse by making sure adults know what they can do to keep children safe. Through their anonymous and confidential online advice and self-help resources they can help you:
Sexual comments.Sexual “jokes” and taunting.
If you’re worried about another adult’s behaviour
Domestic Abuse - Operation Encompass
The purpose of Operation Encompass is to safeguard and support children and young people who have been involved in, or witness to a domestic incident. Domestic abuse impacts on children in a number of ways. Children are at increased risk of physical injury during an incident, either by accident or because they attempt to intervene. Even when not directly injured, children are greatly distressed by witnessing the physical and emotional suffering of a parent. To find out more about what is considered to be a domestic incident please take a look at the guidance from the Met Police on their website: https://www.met.police.uk/advice/advice-and-information/daa/domestic-abuse/what-is-domestic-abuse/
Operation Encompass has been created to highlight this situation. It is the implementation of key partnership working between the police and schools. The aim of sharing information with local schools is to allow key adults i.e. DSL or Deputy DSL the opportunity of engaging with the child and to provide access to support that allows them to remain in a safe but secure familiar environment.

Our Wellbeing
Wellbeing at Islamia Primary School
Parents
Parents play an integral role in the wellbeing of their children. We collaborate with families to create a supportive network through:
Access to information and resources: Providing information about local services which can help families who may be facing problems.
Open communication: Fostering a culture where parents feel comfortable sharing concerns.
Faith-inspired tools: Delivering parent halaqas and Encouraging families to use powerful duas, such as the one taught by the Prophet (peace be upon him):
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief, weakness and laziness, miserliness and cowardice, the burden of debts and the oppression of men." (Sunan Abu Dawood)
Together Towards Wellbeing
At Islamic Primary School, our mission is to nurture a thriving community where every individual can achieve their potential, inspired by the principles of Islam. By aligning with the WHO's holistic understanding of wellbeing and Islamic teachings, we strive to provide a safe, nurturing, and spiritually uplifting environment for all.
If you would like more information or support regarding mental health and wellbeing, please contact admin@islamia.brent.sch.uk
